title: Zacchaeus and the Comparison with Rahab
english: A word concerning Zacchaeus by Amphilochius, bishop of Iconium. Nothing directs the soul toward joy as much as the fear of God, the avoidance of evils, the path of repentance, and the manner of confession.

Therefore even today David blessed those obtaining the forgiveness of sins (Psalm 32:1), while at once presenting the philanthropy of Christ and at once preparing the sinners to run toward repentance. Blessed, he says, are those from whom lawlessness was forgiven and from whom sins were covered (Psalm 32:1). Therefore, let a former tax collector run toward the chaste springs of the salvation of Christ.

There is no receiving a solution from evils nor obtaining blessedness without it, even if you should say prophet, apostle, or evangelist. For all drew from the same spring. In the prophets, David himself, even now being a prophet after adultery, is so because of the grace of the one who forgave. In the apostles, Peter and Paul; for the one, after the denial, holds the keys of the kingdom, and the other, after the persecution of the Gentiles, became an apostle, having changed the Jewish zeal into an evangelical manner.

For in the gospels I know not only Matthew being saved from tax collectors, but also two others with him: of whom one, praying so as to strike the chest, the treasure of evils, from not daring to lift up hands to holy things, from wetting from below, was not only justified but also crowned according to a Pharisee; but Zacchaeus, having climbed upon the tree on which he had stood many times, watching lest any of the merchants might pass by unknowingly so that he might not remain without wealth, watched lest the merchant of heaven and earth, bringing the treasure of the asylum of the kingdom, might pass him by. In order that we may not entirely mix the histories of the tax collectors, if it seems good, taking Zacchaeus alone today, I expand the word for the purpose of a treatise. Having gone out, he says, Jesus was passing through Jericho and behold, a man named (Luke 19:1)...

Zacchaeus also was a tax collector. The evangelist does not mention Jericho simply, but says that God, having thought well of a tax collector in the house. But the matter was unbelievable. He sets before us the pattern, so that, having remembered Rahab the prostitute, we may not be estranged from the reversal of Zacchaeus the stranger. For this reason, therefore, he remembered Jericho, so that having taken Rahab the prostitute into mind, we might compare the manner of both salvations.

For just as Rahab the prostitute received Joshua the son of Nun as a spy and hid him, so also Zacchaeus the tax collector received the true Jesus, who scouts our mind, and nourished him in the house. That woman received Joshua the son of Nun, who brought the people into the land of promise; this man receives the true Jesus, who [is] into the kingdom of heaven, etc. That woman received Joshua the son of Nun [lacuna] this man receives the true Jesus, who laid the foundation of the Jews' temple; for not, he says, shall a stone remain upon a stone here that shall not be destroyed (Matt 21:42). That woman received Joshua the son of Nun, who brought the people through the Jordan into a land flowing with milk and honey (Exod 3:8); this man receives the true Jesus, who brings the believers through baptism to where eye has not seen and ear has not heard and which has not ascended upon the heart of man (1 Cor 2:9). That woman received Joshua the son of Nun, who brought the treasure out of the earth upon a wood; this man receives the true Jesus, who received the thief into paradise (Luke 23:43). [lacuna]

The spring of Jericho was formerly a mother of strife, a nourisher of barrenness, having water that is incomplete. For indeed the stream had an unmeasured flow, like oil flowing without sound, but the sight of the waters sent away the thirsty ones who were looking; for the drink was not without danger to those in need; for the pool had destruction. For the beauty of the spring moved those passing by toward a run, but the fear of harm cut back the readiness.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
